root_cause.text: The driver used `urb->transfer_buffer_length` (the allocated buffer size) instead of `urb->actual_length` (the actual received data size) when validating message boundaries, and lacked a check for the minimum header length before dereferencing the message structure, leading to potential out-of-bounds reads.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (start > urb->transfer_buffer_length)` to `if (start > urb->actual_length)` and adds a new check `if (start + CPC_MSG_HEADER_LEN > urb->actual_length)` before accessing `msg->type`, ensuring both that the header fits and that the next message offset does not exceed actual received data. The commit message states "actual_length is the size of the buffer passed to the driver, not the transfer_buffer_length".
